attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article, endorsed. Not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: The revision keeps 'exact same corporate entity', the 'mere months' timing, the $30M figure and the 'from what I can tell' qualifier. This is a historical account, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: The readings of 'disappearing', 'mere months' and 'after raising $30M' are ordinary. The result depends on how withdrawal and continuity are read, and the speaker gave no measure for either. The epistemic qualifier is noted but does not stop the account being checked.

evidence.note: Rabbit's own disclosure of $30M raised to date as of Jan 2024. It fits the funding milestone, but it is a company disclosure dated before the contract's May endpoint, and it says nothing about entity continuity.
Reports the NFT history. Rabbit's statement frames GAMA as a project Lyu left. It does not settle legal continuity or when GAMA withdrew from users.
Shows GAMA code was open-sourced in Nov 2023. It does not date when support for users stopped.
Confirms R1 deliveries by April 2024 and mentions a further funding round with no amount. It is silent on continuity with GAMA.

reviews.rationale: The $30M milestone and the R1 sales are documented, but by company disclosure only. The central claim that this is the same legal entity is not established: the name-change filing could not be read. The timing of GAMA's withdrawal from users is also not established. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article, endorsed.

semantics.note: Faithful to the statement. Dropping 'alleged' before LAM is a rhetorical change only and does not alter what the claim commits to.

contract.note: Reading launch as consumer availability, and reading LAM reliability at the level of the delivered product, are both ordinary readings. Excluding staged demos is fair.

evidence.note: Pre-launch company FAQ placing public release of Teach Mode later in the year. It corroborates the claim but predates launch.
The Verge's hands-on testing in the launch period: Uber and DoorDash repeatedly failed, and Spotify was unreliable.
Tom's Guide found repeated errors when ordering rides and food, and lists Teach Mode as a future feature. It also reports some successes.
Demos at the launch event worked, and Teach Mode was shown only as testing. Demos are outside the contract's measure.

reviews.rationale: Rabbit's own documentation and an independent review both show Teach Mode was not generally available at launch. Hands-on reviews from the launch period record repeated failures of the advertised Uber and DoorDash actions. Successful demos and occasional successes do not show the system was dependable. Both named parts of the claim hold.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article, endorsed.

semantics.note: Price, shipping and review sentiment are all preserved.

contract.note: Rounding $199 to $200, treating 'started shipping' as deliveries having begun, and judging prominent completed reviews by their overall verdicts are ordinary readings.

evidence.note: Company disclosure of customers picking up orders in person in April 2024, showing distribution had begun.
The Verge's completed review (May 2) gives the $199 price and an unfavorable verdict.
WIRED's completed review (May 3) rated the device 3/10 at $199, with an unfavorable verdict.
Engadget's completed review (May 3) tells readers not to buy it.
Favorable early impressions from the launch event. These are not a completed review, so they do not outweigh the later verdicts.

reviews.rationale: The price was $199, and deliveries to customers had begun in April 2024. Three prominent completed reviews published before May 6 were clearly unfavorable. TechCrunch's more positive early impressions came from the launch event, not a completed review. All three elements hold.
